summary.title: 2.3 Emerald Rapids: 5th-Generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors
summary.one_liner: Learn what changed in Intel's 5th-Gen Xeon Scalable (Emerald Rapids) design: up to 64 cores, over 300MB shared L3, faster DDR5 and I/O links, and its performance and idle-power gains over 4th-Gen Xeon.
takeaways: Emerald Rapids supports up to 64 cores, over 300MB shared L3 cache, and 8 DDR5 channels at 5600MT/s with 1DPC.
It uses 32GT/s PCIe/CXL lanes and 20GT/s UPI lanes, built as two die in a multichip package.
Claimed gains over 4th-Gen Xeon at iso power: 18% for general integer workloads and 24% for floating-point workloads.
Manufacturing uses the Intel 7 process, tuned for server use, giving +3% frequency/W over the prior process revision.
Idle power savings came from improved FIVR losses at low utilization, active idle detection, and package C6 power reduction.
summary.summary: This is a short technical paper section from IEEE Xplore describing the 5th-Generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors (Emerald Rapids). It lists the headline specs: up to 64 cores, more than 300MB shared L3 cache, eight DDR5 channels at 5600MT/s, and PCIe/CXL and UPI links, built from two die in a multichip package. It attributes the reported 18% integer and 24% floating-point gains at iso power to an improved core, process tuning, more cores, bigger cache, faster memory, die reductions, and idle power work. The page does not give a deeper benchmark breakdown beyond this abstract.
